counterfactual_missing_items: No susceptibility testing to confirm antibiotic resistance
Lesion progression despite antibiotics does not prove resistance
decisive_items: inflamed, infiltrating, necrotic lesion over the implant site
A swab of the lesion grew Staphylococcus epidermidis
response.rationale: C1 is the most complete: it names the pacemaker pocket infection and adds the cultured organism, matching both the implant-site lesion and the S. epidermidis swab. R1 is correct but lacks the organism in the label; R3 has the organism but misses the pocket anatomy; R2 infers resistance without susceptibility evidence.

rejected.why: Antibiotic resistance is not established; no susceptibility testing is reported and lesion progression can occur in pocket infection despite empiric antibiotics.
Identifies the organism but omits the pacemaker pocket/implant site, which is the key anatomical diagnosis.
